prerequisites: Knowledge of fundamentals of solid mechanics: tensor analysis, static laws, concepts of displacement, strain and stress, dependencies between these quantities in an elastic medium, the ability to calculate displacements and stress in a member.

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows: how to determine stress and displacement in rotating disks, pipes and thick-walled tanks.
Student knows the theory of thin-walled axisymmetric shells loaded with pressure.
Student knows the basics of fatigue of material and fatigue of simple construction elements.
Student has practical skills in: performing basic strength tests.
Student has practical skills in measuring the plain state of strain using tensometers (strain gauges).
Student has practical skills in determining the basic elasticity constants: Young modulus, Poisson ratio and Kirchhoff modulus.
Social competencies: independent research and critical evaluation of the found sources.
Social competencies: objective evaluation of arguments, rational explanation and justification of the student’s viewpoint using knowledge of the strength of materials.
Social competencies: conforming to the academic principles.

syllabus_topics: Symmetrically loaded circular plates. Rectangular plates.
Time and temperature dependent loads – fatigue, creep, relaxation.
Finite Element Method (FEM) – introduction, shape functions.
Tensile test in metals and plastics.
Buckling of slender members. Compression test.
teaching_methods: Lectures supported with audiovisual aids when necessary.
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
